interactions.label: The 'double burden of malnutrition' described in the case of the pregnant woman

params.question: The 'double burden of malnutrition' described in the case of the pregnant woman from Rajasthan refers to the coexistence of which two patterns in India?

answers.text: Iron deficiency in women and calcium deficiency in children

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Iron and calcium deficiency are both forms of undernutrition. The double burden refers to undernutrition AND overnutrition coexisting simultaneously in the same country.

answers.text: Undernutrition in rural populations and overnutrition in urban populations

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct! India faces micronutrient deficiencies and stunting predominantly in rural areas alongside rising obesity and metabolic syndrome in urban populations — both existing at the same time.

answers.text: Protein deficiency in adults and vitamin deficiency in children

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: These are both forms of undernutrition. The 'double burden' specifically describes the simultaneous occurrence of undernutrition and overnutrition across different population segments.

answers.text: Childhood malnutrition and elderly malnutrition

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: The double burden is not defined by age groups. It refers to undernutrition (stunting, wasting, micronutrient deficiencies) coexisting with overnutrition (obesity, metabolic syndrome) across India's population.

overallFeedback.feedback: Review the concept: the double burden refers to undernutrition (rural, micronutrient deficiencies) coexisting with overnutrition (urban, obesity and metabolic syndrome) in the same country.
India's double burden means undernutrition and overnutrition exist side by side — understanding this is essential for community health planning.

interactions.label: A 35-year-old Indian man has a BMI of 24.5 kg/m². Using the Asia-Pacific BMI cut

params.question: A 35-year-old Indian man has a BMI of 24.5 kg/m². Using the Asia-Pacific BMI cut-offs recommended for Indian populations, how would you classify his nutritional status?

answers.text: Underweight — he needs to gain weight

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: A BMI of 24.5 is well above the underweight threshold (below 18.5 by any classification). This patient actually falls into the overweight category by Asia-Pacific standards.

answers.text: Overweight with increased risk — the Asia-Pacific cut-off is 23 or above

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct! The Asia-Pacific cut-offs classify a BMI of 23 or above as overweight with increased cardiometabolic risk. This is lower than the WHO cut-off of 25 because Indians accumulate visceral fat at lower BMIs.

answers.text: Normal weight — his BMI is below the WHO overweight threshold of 25

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: While 24.5 is below the standard WHO overweight cut-off of 25, Indian and Asian populations accumulate visceral fat at lower BMIs. The Asia-Pacific cut-off for overweight is 23, making this patient overweight by the appropriate regional standard.

answers.text: Obese with high risk — the Asia-Pacific cut-off for obesity is 25

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: The Asia-Pacific cut-off for obesity with high risk is 27.5, not 25. At a BMI of 24.5, this patient is classified as overweight (≥23), not obese.

overallFeedback.feedback: Remember: for Indian and Asian populations, the Asia-Pacific cut-offs apply — overweight starts at BMI 23 (not 25) and obesity at 27.5 (not 30), because visceral fat accumulates at lower BMIs.
In Indian clinical practice, always apply the Asia-Pacific BMI cut-offs (overweight ≥23, obese ≥27.5) to account for higher visceral fat deposition at lower BMIs.

interactions.label: In kwashiorkor, body weight appears deceptively close to normal because fluid re

params.question: In kwashiorkor, body weight appears deceptively close to normal because fluid retention from hypoalbuminaemia masks the underlying nutritional deficit.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is true. Kwashiorkor involves protein deficiency → low albumin → oedema (swelling in feet, legs, face). This fluid retention adds body mass, masking the severity of the nutritional deficit and making weight appear deceptively normal.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct! In kwashiorkor, protein deficiency leads to low serum albumin, which causes oedema — fluid leaks from blood vessels into tissues, adding weight. This makes the child's body weight appear near-normal despite severe undernutrition.

interactions.label: Why is prevention through universal salt iodisation, rather than treatment after

params.question: Why is prevention through universal salt iodisation, rather than treatment after birth, the primary strategy against iodine deficiency disorders?

answers.text: Because iodine supplements are prohibitively expensive for mass distribution

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Salt iodisation is actually one of the most cost-effective public health interventions. The reason prevention is prioritised is that the most devastating consequence — cretinism — is irreversible once it occurs.

answers.text: Because iodine deficiency only affects pregnant women, who can be reached through antenatal care

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Iodine deficiency affects entire populations — goitre can occur in anyone. However, the consequences during foetal development (cretinism) are irreversible, which is why universal prevention through fortified salt is essential.

answers.text: Because cretinism causes irreversible brain damage that cannot be treated once it occurs

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct! Cretinism results from iodine deficiency during foetal brain development, causing permanent intellectual disability. No treatment can reverse this after birth, making prevention through universal salt iodisation the only effective approach.

answers.text: Because goitre, once developed, never responds to iodine supplementation

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Goitre can actually regress with adequate iodine supplementation. It is cretinism — irreversible brain damage in babies born to iodine-deficient mothers — that makes prevention the only real solution.

overallFeedback.feedback: The key reason is irreversibility: cretinism (brain damage from foetal iodine deficiency) cannot be treated after birth, making universal prevention through iodised salt the only effective strategy.
Iodine deficiency causes irreversible cretinism in the foetus — since no post-natal treatment exists, universal salt iodisation is one of India's most successful public health preventive measures.

interactions.label: Nutritional surveillance differs from a one-time nutritional survey primarily be

params.question: Nutritional surveillance differs from a one-time nutritional survey primarily because it involves:

answers.text: Collecting data exclusively from hospitals and health centres

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Surveillance collects data from multiple sources: community health workers via the POSHAN Tracker, national surveys, food balance sheets, vital statistics, and sentinel sites like Anganwadi centres — not just hospitals.

answers.text: Using only anthropometric measurements for assessment

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Both surveys and surveillance can use anthropometric measurements. The defining feature of surveillance is its continuous, ongoing nature, not the type of data it collects.

answers.text: Assessing individual patients in a clinical setting

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Surveillance operates at the population level, tracking nutritional trends across communities to inform public health decisions — it is not about individual clinical assessment.

answers.text: Continuous monitoring of a population's nutritional status to inform decisions

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct! Nutritional surveillance is defined as the continuous monitoring of a population's nutritional status so that timely decisions can be made — for early warning, programme monitoring, programme evaluation, and policy planning.

overallFeedback.feedback: The defining feature of nutritional surveillance is the word 'continuous' — it is ongoing population-level monitoring, unlike a one-time survey snapshot.
Surveillance is a continuous system feeding data into decisions — early warning, programme monitoring, programme evaluation, and policy planning.

interactions.label: While inspecting a roadside food stall, you notice the vendor storing raw chicke

params.question: While inspecting a roadside food stall, you notice the vendor storing raw chicken in direct contact with cooked rice. Which of the WHO's five keys to safer food is being violated?

answers.text: Separate raw and cooked foods

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct! Separating raw and cooked foods prevents cross-contamination — a leading cause of foodborne illness. Raw chicken may harbour Salmonella, which can contaminate the cooked rice through direct contact.

answers.text: Keep clean

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: 'Keep clean' refers to hand hygiene, surface sanitisation, and keeping pests away from food areas. While important, the specific violation here — raw meat touching cooked food — is a failure to separate raw from cooked.

answers.text: Cook food thoroughly

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: 'Cook thoroughly' means ensuring food reaches a core temperature of at least 70°C. The issue here is not undercooking but the contact between raw and cooked items, which risks cross-contamination.

answers.text: Use safe water and safe raw materials

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: This key refers to the quality and safety of water and raw ingredients used in preparation. The problem in this scenario is the physical contact between raw chicken and cooked rice — a separation failure.

overallFeedback.feedback: The five keys are: keep clean, separate raw and cooked, cook thoroughly, keep at safe temperatures, and use safe water and raw materials. Storing raw chicken with cooked rice violates the separation principle.
Cross-contamination from raw to cooked foods is a leading cause of foodborne illness — separating them is one of the WHO's five keys to safer food.
